issues.description: Field 'stock' in SealSaloon: the problem statement first instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon's stock in the instance constructor (constructor takes no parameters and should set default values), but the requirements later state that 'stock' must be static/shared across all SealSaloon instances. The solution declares and initializes a static field (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This contradiction (instance-initialized vs static/shared) in the problem statement versus the solution/UML will confuse students about where and how to create/initialize the stock field and whether methods that manage it must be static.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intent explicit and consistent: either (A) require an instance field 'stock' and instruct students to initialize it in the constructor (remove the note saying it must be static), or (B) require a static shared 'stock' and instruct students to initialize it at the declaration or in a static initializer (remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor). Update the UML, problem text, and any example code to match the chosen option.

issues.description: Method name for adding a StockIngredient to Stock differs across artifacts: the UML/problem statement specifies addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient): void, the template Stock class provides addItem(StockIngredient) (method name 'addItem'), while the reference solution implements addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation will confuse students and can cause compile errors if the SealSaloon implementation expects the UML name but the provided template uses a different name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API name across all artifacts. Preferred options: (1) Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) so the starter code matches the UML and solution, or (2) update the UML/problem statement to use addItem if that name is preferred. As a minimal compatibility fix, add a delegating method in the template: addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) { addItem(ingredient); } so both names exist.
